name: Nepalgunj
blurb: A hot border city on the Terai plains and the air hub for western Nepal. Flights to Juphal, Jumla, Talcha and Simikot leave soon after dawn, so almost every Dolpo or Rara trip includes a night here.
tip: Stay near the airport, which is several kilometres north of the centre; mountain flights board very early.

name: Juphal
blurb: A hillside village in Dolpa with the short, sloping airstrip that serves the whole district. Treks to Phoksundo Lake and Upper Dolpo start and end here.
tip: Flights go only in the calm of early morning. If yours is cancelled, put your name down for the next day before you leave the airstrip.

name: Dunai
blurb: Headquarters of Dolpa district, a single paved bazaar beside the Thuli Bheri. Restricted-area permits are registered here, and it has the last proper shops and the district hospital.

name: Suligad
blurb: The entrance to Shey Phoksundo National Park, where the Suligad river meets the Thuli Bheri between Juphal and Dunai. Permits are checked here before you turn north into the gorge.

name: Chhepka
blurb: The first lodge stop in the Suligad gorge, a few houses among walnut trees and small fields beside the river. Its altitude is listed anywhere from 2,600 to 2,838 m.

name: Rechi
blurb: A small riverside settlement with a lodge or two in the middle of the gorge, at about 2,940 m. Useful for breaking the long stage between Chhepka and Chunuwar.

name: Chunuwar
blurb: Lodges, a school and a traditional Tibetan medicine clinic a little above Sumduwa, where the Pungmo Khola joins the main valley. It is the last stop before the climb to Phoksundo Lake.

name: Phoksundo Waterfall Viewpoint
blurb: A ridge on the trail between Chunuwar and Ringmo, at roughly 3,800 m, with the first view of Phoksundo Lake and of the 167 m waterfall where its outflow drops into the gorge.

name: Ringmo
blurb: A Bon village of flat-roofed stone houses on the old landslide dam that holds back Phoksundo Lake. It has the only lodges at the lake and a national park post.
tip: Bon chortens and mani walls are passed anticlockwise, the reverse of Buddhist practice.

name: Phoksundo Lake
blurb: Nepal's deepest lake, about 145 m, filling a steep-sided valley at 3,612 m. Its colour shifts from turquoise to deep blue through the day, and apart from Ringmo its shore is empty.

name: Tshowa Gompa
blurb: A Bon monastery on a bluff above the eastern shore of Phoksundo Lake, about half an hour's walk from Ringmo. It is said to be around 900 years old.

name: Phoksundo Lake Viewpoint
blurb: The high point of the cliff trail above the lake's western shore, at about 4,040 m. It gives the classic view down the length of the water to Ringmo.

name: Phoksundo Khola Camp
blurb: A camping ground among birch and willow on the flood plain where the Phoksundo Khola enters the head of the lake. It is the first night out from Ringmo on the way to Shey.

name: Kang La Base Camp
blurb: A high pasture camp at about 4,400 m at the head of the gorge below the Kang La, called Phoksundo Bhanjyang on many itineraries. Some crews camp higher to shorten the pass day.

name: Kang La (Dolpo)
blurb: The pass between the Phoksundo and Shey valleys, about 5,350 m and also known as the Nangdalo La. The southern side is steep slate scree, often under snow. It is the high point of the Upper Dolpo route.

name: Shey Gompa
blurb: A small red-walled monastery at the meeting of two rivers, below the Crystal Mountain that pilgrims circle on foot. A few houses and a campsite stand beside it. Heights from 4,160 to 4,500 m are quoted.

name: Saldang La
blurb: The pass between Shey and Namgung, also called the Sela La or Gela La. Itineraries quote anything from 5,010 to 5,200 m; about 5,100 m is a fair working figure.

name: Namgung
blurb: A tiny village with an old red-stone monastery built against a cliff, in a side gorge between the Saldang La and Saldang. Agencies often list it as Namduna Gaun, sometimes at an unlikely 4,800 m.

name: Saldang
blurb: The largest village in Upper Dolpo, spread along terraces above the Nagon Khola, with several monasteries and a long history of trade with Tibet. Heights from 3,620 to about 3,900 m are quoted for it.

name: Sibu
blurb: A line of stone houses, chortens and barley fields beside the river south of Saldang, used as the camp before the approach to the Jeng La. Published altitudes vary widely, from about 3,940 to 4,560 m.

name: Jeng La Phedi
blurb: Pasture at the northern foot of the Jeng La where crews camp before the crossing. The exact site moves with water and grazing, and heights from about 4,400 to 4,900 m appear in print.

name: Jeng La
blurb: A pass of about 5,090 m linking the Saldang side of Upper Dolpo with the Tarap valley. The climb from the north is short and steep, and in clear weather the Dhaulagiri range lines the southern horizon.

name: Tokyu
blurb: A string of hamlets with a monastery at the head of the Tarap valley, at about 4,200 m. The trail from the Jeng La and the one from the Numa La meet here.

name: Dho Tarap
blurb: The main village of the Tarap valley, a compact group of stone houses among barley fields at around 4,000 m. It has Bon and Buddhist monasteries close by, a school, a few shops and simple places to stay.

name: Tarap Khola Camp
blurb: A riverside meadow, known as Kamakharka, where the open Tarap valley narrows into its gorge. It is the usual first camp on the way down from Dho Tarap.

name: Laini Odar
blurb: A camping spot in the lower Tarap gorge, named for its rock overhang and also written Lahini or Laina Odar. Listed heights range from about 3,160 to 3,370 m.

name: Tarakot
blurb: An old fortress village on a hill above the Thuli Bheri, once the seat of a small kingdom on the trade route. The trail into the Tarap gorge leaves the main valley a little upstream.

name: Jumla
blurb: The main town of the Karnali, in a wide valley of rice terraces and apple orchards at about 2,370 m. It has an airstrip, a teaching hospital, banks and the last real bazaar before Rara.

name: Chere Chaur
blurb: Broad meadows on the ridge north of Jumla with a view back over the Tila valley. A common first night out, and the point where the Sinja and Danphe Lagna trails part.

name: Jaljala Pass
blurb: A grassy pass at about 3,580 m between Chere Chaur and the Sinja side, leading onto the high pasture of Jaljala Chaur where horses are grazed in summer.

name: Chalachaur
blurb: A village with meadows and a few simple places to stay on the descent from the Jaljala pass towards the Sinja valley, at about 2,980 m.

name: Sinja
blurb: A village on the Sinja Khola that was the capital of the Khasa kingdom from the twelfth to the fourteenth century and is regarded as the cradle of the Nepali language. The Kanakasundari temple stands on a knoll above it.

name: Ghorosingha
blurb: A clearing with a campsite and very basic shelter in the forest between Sinja and Rara, listed at 3,050 to 3,190 m. It is the last stop before the ridge above the lake.

name: Rara Lake
blurb: Nepal's largest lake, about 10.8 square kilometres and up to 167 m deep, set at 2,990 m among pine, spruce and juniper. The park headquarters and a few simple lodges are on the northern shore.
tip: Mornings are calmest; by midday wind ruffles the water and the reflections go.

name: Murma Top
blurb: The hilltop above Murma village at the lake's western end, somewhere between 3,630 and 3,780 m depending on the source. It is the one place from which the whole of Rara Lake is visible.

name: Pina
blurb: A farming village on the main trail between Jumla and Rara, at the northern foot of the Ghurchi Lagna. It has basic lodges and a small shop.

name: Ghurchi Lagna
blurb: A forested pass at about 3,450 m on the divide between Jumla and Mugu districts. In clear weather it looks north over the Mugu Karnali valley to the peaks on the Tibetan border.

name: Bumra
blurb: A village above the Sinja Khola on the direct trail between Jumla and Rara, with a couple of basic lodges. It is the usual overnight stop between the two passes.

name: Danphe Lagna
blurb: The higher of the two passes between Jumla and the Sinja Khola, usually given as 3,691 m, in forest of birch, spruce and rhododendron. It is named after the danphe, Nepal's national bird, which lives here.

name: Talcha
blurb: The airstrip for Mugu district, on a hillside two to three hours' walk east of Rara Lake. Flights from Nepalgunj make the lake reachable in a day when the weather holds.

name: Gamgadhi
blurb: Headquarters of Mugu district, a small bazaar on a ridge above the Mugu Karnali, below the Talcha airstrip. It has basic hotels, shops and a district hospital, and is where the rough road from Jumla ends.

name: Surkhet
blurb: The capital of Karnali province, officially Birendranagar, in a broad valley at about 700 m. The Karnali Highway to Jumla starts here, which makes it the road gateway to Rara when flights are grounded.

name: Dhangadhi
blurb: The largest city of the far-western Terai and the arrival point for Khaptad and the hills beyond. Flights from Kathmandu land here; buses and jeeps for the hills leave from Attariya, just to the north.

name: Silgadhi
blurb: The old hill bazaar of Doti, on a ridge above Dipayal and the Seti river, known for its Shaileshwari temple. Both the walk and the jeep track to Khaptad start here.

name: Jhigrana
blurb: The entrance to Khaptad National Park on the Doti side, with a park office, an army post and a few simple lodges at the forest edge. A jeep track reaches it from Silgadhi.

name: Bichpani
blurb: A rest stop with a tea house and shelter in the forest roughly halfway up from Jhigrana to the plateau. Sources give its height as 2,900 to 3,020 m.

name: Khaptad
blurb: The park headquarters on the Khaptad plateau at about 3,020 m: offices, an army post and a few basic lodges at the edge of a wide meadow. Khaptad Baba's ashram and the Tribeni temple are a short walk away.
